items.item_text: Five (5) years of trade experience. Assignments inside the substation may only be performed by individuals with hands-on switchgear training or the ability to complete switchgear training within one year of hire or by those working under the direct supervision of a qualified substation operator.

Assist the Substation Foreman in the operation and maintenance of the campus electrical substation. Troubleshoot electrical problems by locating and determining electrical malfunctions using test instruments such as ammeter, multimeter, circuit tracer, etc.

Repair malfunctions by such methods as replacing burnt out elements and fuses, bypassing or replacing defective wiring, cleaning and troubleshooting motors and controls, and replacing fixture ballasts.
Test electrical equipment such as motors and heaters for safety and efficiency. Bend and install wire-mold, EMT, and rigid conduit.
Install fixtures, motors, and other electrical equipment.
Repair motor controls and VFD troubleshooting
Inspect circuits and wiring for specified shielding and grounding and repairing or rewiring systems according to building codes and safety regulations.
Repair mechanical, pneumatic, hydraulic, and electronic components of electrical equipment.
Read and interpret blueprints, electrical schematics, maintenance manuals and specifications. Troubleshoot existing installations and install new electrical systems based on this information.
Support the Electric Shop and Central Facilities Services performing other duties as assigned.
Maintain as-built drawings of work undertaken to depict actual construction variances from design drawings.
Learn BAS controls as required by updated technologies.
Perform other related duties as assigned.
